bindings.label: A painful area on the right lateral chest present for 2 weeks
Patient is a woman in her 50s; she was taking prednisone 10 mg daily and had not used any topical medications

Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful
Physical examination demonstrated a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest
Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses both rank chronic refractory dermatosis as the most probable diagnosis
Biopsy pathology report lacks detailed histomorphology, special stains, and immunohistochemistry; HSV/VZV PCR and cultures are not available
Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses both name refractory eczematous dermatitis as the most probable working diagnosis
